title: September 11, 2001
subject: histoire
description: On **September 11, 2001**, nineteen Al-Qaeda terrorists hijacked four planes. The deadliest attack in American history opened the era of the war on terror.

hero.hook: A September morning that closed the post-Cold War world and opened a century of wars.

blocks.text: On Tuesday, **September 11, 2001**, nineteen members of **[[Al-Qaeda]]**, the terrorist group founded by **Osama bin Laden**, hijacked four planes. Two hit the **World Trade Center** in New York, a third the **Pentagon**, the headquarters of American defense. The fourth crashed in Pennsylvania after the passengers fought back.
The toll: **2,977** dead. Beyond the horror of the day, the attack ended any hope of a calmer world order and set off a chain of conflicts that still shape the 21st century.

**Osama bin Laden**, a Saudi billionaire turned jihadist leader, founded **[[Al-Qaeda]]** in the late **1980s**, in the wake of the **[[Soviet-Afghan War (1979-1989)]]**. After the Soviet withdrawal he denounced the American military presence in **[[Saudi Arabia]]** and decided to strike the West.

blocks.caption: Osama bin Laden, founder of Al-Qaeda

blocks.text: The warnings piled up: a bombing at the World Trade Center in **1993**, the East African embassies in **1998**, the destroyer USS Cole in **2000**. But the wall between the CIA and the FBI, the American intelligence services, kept anyone from tying the threads together in time.
The 19 hijackers spent about **$400,000** on an attack whose total economic cost would run past **$2 trillion**.

At **8:46** a.m., American Airlines Flight 11 hit the North Tower. At **9:03** a.m., United 175 struck the South Tower live on television. At **9:37** a.m., American 77 hit the Pentagon. At **10:03** a.m., United 93 crashed in Pennsylvania.

blocks.caption: The Twin Towers of the World Trade Center, the main targets of the attacks

blocks.text: The towers came down, the South at **9:59** a.m., the North at **10:28** a.m. American airspace was closed for the first time ever. Those images became the founding trauma of a generation.

In October **2001**, Operation **[[Enduring Freedom]]** targeted Afghanistan: destroy Al-Qaeda and topple the **[[Taliban]]**, the Islamist movement that had sheltered bin Laden. Kabul fell fast. The war lasted twenty years.

In March **2003**, without a UN mandate, the United States launched [[The Iraq War]], accusing the dictator **[[Saddam Hussein]]** of holding weapons of mass destruction. The charge was false, and the country slid into chaos. At **[[Guantanamo]]**, an American base in Cuba, detainees were held outside ordinary law. Bin Laden was killed in Pakistan on **May 1, 2011**.

In the United States, the **PATRIOT Act**, an emergency law, widened surveillance enormously. Europe followed. Airports changed forever. Ground Zero, the site of the fallen towers, became a memorial and a symbol of resilience.
The wars that followed killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions. Global terrorism, now more scattered, uses the tools of globalization to fight it.

events.title: The attacks
events.detail: 2,977 people killed in the United States.

blocks.text: **September 11, 2001** turned a threat into a global war: interventions in Afghanistan and Iraq, and a lasting security turn inside the democracies themselves.
